scope: Korean course unique indices 0..499, Romanian and Finnish authoring; 1000 records
courseSteps: K1..K10 are course stages, not official proficiency grades 1..6.

contextPolicy.existingPeopleGender: unspecified unless explicit in the same source; names and occupations are not evidence
contextPolicy.number: source-preserved; plural/singular grammar not used to invent omitted participants
contextPolicy.referents: Korean examples and reported-speech embedded subjects take precedence over abbreviated English glosses
contextPolicy.romanianGrammaticalGender: Generic elev/prieten/medic grammatical masculine does not set an existing character’s semantic gender; persoană is grammatically feminine without asserting female identity.
contextPolicy.explicitGender: 203/204 woman-speaker older-brother/older-sister and 309/325 grandmother explicitly supplied by source

issues.reason: Pronunciation teaching guidance has not been reviewed by a Korean phonetics expert. ㄹ approximation, aspiration and tense-throat/skate comparison are translated faithfully; no new validity approval is asserted.

English friend said coming conflates the omitted reporter with embedded subject 친구. Korean establishes that a friend comes; reporter and addressee remain unspecified. Target glosses keep the reporter impersonal, without setting gender.
English letter written well adds well, absent from 글씨가 써져요. Both native glosses omit that unsupported manner claim; 글씨가 써져요 is preserved.
Affix-causative lesson includes analytic 보여 주다 in its examples. Translated as supplied, without reclassifying the shared source.
Tense/register ending summaries are simplified teaching descriptions, not exhaustive grammar rules. No expert review claimed.
Pare să se bucure uses a gender-neutral verbal rendering of looks happy. Close emotional meaning but Romanian native pedagogical review may prefer another neutral formulation.
Persoana mai mică dintre frați avoids assigning sex to 동생. Correct younger-sibling relation; Romanian native review is recommended for fluency.

limits: AI authoring and surface checks only; no native-speaker, teacher or phonetics-expert approval.
No claim of target-language automatic answer-grading support.
